pages.critique:
All four contract criteria now pass. The table survives at every viewport (no more content loss), and interacting with it still works correctly post-fix: selecting entity_type=RiskBandAssignment and clicking Apply correctly re-queried and narrowed 8 entries down to 2 matching rows (screenshot-verified), matching pre-fix filtering behavior.

visual_hierarchy (7/10, was 5/10): h2 'Audit log' > h3 'Filters'/'Entries' panels > uppercase th labels > row data holds up consistently now across all three widths -- the Entries panel always has real, organized data to show. Not scored higher because at 768px/375px the table requires horizontal scrolling to reach the ACTION/DETAILS_JSON columns (visible cut off at the right edge of the screenshot) rather than a purpose-built narrow-viewport layout like Holdings' card fallback -- functional and legible, but denser/less elegant than the sibling screen.

accessibility (8/10, was 5/10): the critical regression is resolved -- the table's semantic markup (scope=col headers, etc.) is present in the DOM at every viewport, so a keyboard/screen-reader user on a narrow viewport can now reach every audit entry via the table's horizontal scroll instead of finding nothing. Labels, tab order (#actor_id -> #entity_type), and Enter-submits-the-form all remain correct, and #actor_id/Apply/Clear still show the branded blue focus-visible outline. One pre-existing minor gap is unchanged and not re-scored down for it: the #entity_type <select> still isn't covered by global.css's `input:focus-visible, button:focus-visible, a:focus-visible` selector (line ~76-81), so it still falls back to the browser's default outline instead of the branded ring -- worth a follow-up but no longer blocking, since it's cosmetic-inconsistency rather than content-loss.

responsiveness (7/10, was 3/10, meets the 7 bar for this criterion): both bugs are fixed -- confirmed via document.documentElement.scrollWidth (1280/768/375) exactly equal to clientWidth at every width, i.e. zero page-level horizontal overflow anywhere, and the table itself remains visible and usable (via its own internal horizontal scrollbar) rather than vanishing. Not scored higher than 7 because E3-S4 has no purpose-built narrow-viewport layout (unlike Holdings' card list) -- a horizontally-scrollable dense table is an acceptable, functional fallback for a compliance-tool screen but not as polished a mobile experience as the sibling page.

interaction_feedback (7/10, was 6/10): filtering (entity_type=RiskBandAssignment: 8 -> 2 matching entries, count text and rows both updated correctly), Previous/Next disabled-state logic, and Enter-key submission all continue to work exactly as before at 1280px -- and now that consistency extends to 768px/375px too, since the table (and therefore visible feedback about filter results) no longer disappears at those widths.

pages.critique:
This is the strongest of the two Group F screens and is genuinely well executed. visual_hierarchy (7/10): clear h2 'Holdings & drift' + sub-copy, two well-separated panels ('Portfolio summary' dl and 'By asset class' table/cards), right-aligned tabular-nums monospace numbers for scannability, and the out-of-tolerance row/card (FI_GOV, drift -6.66 vs 5.00 threshold) is unmistakably flagged with a peach background and border matching the mockup's intent. Deductions: the table shows only asset_class_code ('FI_GOV') and never asset_class_name ('Government Fixed Income') even though the API response and mockup both carry it -- a retail customer sees jargon codes instead of plain-language labels; and exceeds_threshold is rendered as bare text 'true'/'false' rather than the mockup's rounded pill/badge ('true - out of tolerance' / 'false'), so the flag relies more on background-tint alone than the mockup's redundant text+shape+color treatment.

accessibility (8/10): semantic table with scope=col headers, tabular-nums for alignment, data-breach="true" attribute on both the <tr> and the mobile <article class="card"> for reliable programmatic/CSS targeting, comfortable text contrast throughout (#5c5c66 muted labels on white/#f4f4f5), and the same data survives intact into the card layout at narrow widths (every dt/dl pair is preserved, nothing is dropped). The exceeds_threshold state is conveyed by both a color/background cue and the literal word 'true'/'false' in text, so it doesn't rely on color alone.

responsiveness (9/10, required >=7, the raised bar for this story): this is the mockup's designated single responsive-breakpoint screen (BRD §5.3) and it delivers exactly as specified -- confirmed by document.documentElement.scrollWidth === clientWidth at all three widths (1280/768/375, no horizontal overflow anywhere). Table layout renders at 1280px; at 768px and 375px the .tablewrap is hidden and .cards renders instead, with each asset class as its own bordered card containing a 2-column current_value/current_percent/target_percent/drift_percent grid -- a clean, accurate implementation of the exact breakpoint behavior the contract calls out.

interaction_feedback (7/10): this view is primarily read-only display (no filter controls in scope for E6-S5), so feedback is judged on the breach-highlighting affordance (instant, unambiguous, no interaction required) and the responsive transition itself, which is immediate and correct when resizing between widths. Not scored higher only because there are no loading/error/empty states observed in either pass -- the empty-state component (EmptyState.tsx / AC3) exists per the architecture checks but wasn't exercised live (no zero-holdings fixture account was available), so empty-state interaction feedback specifically remains unverified rather than confirmed.

Remaining minor, non-blocking gap: the #entity_type <select> still doesn't get the branded focus-visible outline that inputs/buttons get (falls back to browser default) -- cosmetic, not a functional or content-access issue.

summary.overall:
PASS (iteration 4) -- all 7 of 7 pages now PASS their contract bars. Both of iteration 3's remaining defects are fixed and re-verified live with the same quantitative methodology that originally found them: (1) TemplateEditor's Version History table now correctly grows in place after a successful Publish, with zero manual reload, confirmed by a live DOM poll (11 -> 12 rows) alongside the success toast in the same render -- generator-G-fix3 switched it from a re-fetch-via-loadHistory() pattern to the same direct local-state-append pattern RuleEditor.tsx and AssetClasses.tsx already used, eliminating the race rather than patching around it. (2) Both TemplateEditor (was 65px) and RuleEditor (was 91px, the worst regression found in this entire multi-iteration review) now measure exactly 0px of horizontal overflow at 375px, confirmed via document.documentElement.scrollWidth === clientWidth === 375 plus full-page screenshots showing every row's input and Remove button fitting cleanly within the viewport. As a bonus, this iteration also live-drove RuleEditor's actual Publish-click-to-history-update behavior for the first time (previously only its enable/disable gate had been re-confirmed in iteration 3) and found it working correctly, closing out that page's last open question.

Group G's full journey across 4 iterations: iteration 1 found a total frontend routing gap (all 7 pages unreachable, 0/10 everywhere); iteration 2 found the routing fix worked but surfaced 3 missing backend GET endpoints blocking 5 of 7 pages; iteration 3 found those endpoints fixed and 5 of 7 pages passing, but surfaced 2 new, narrower defects (a broken version-history refresh, and significant 375px overflow) unique to the two admin editor screens; iteration 4 confirms both of those are now fixed, with no new defects found. All 7 pages -- Questionnaire, RiskResult, Goals, Rebalancing, TemplateEditor, RuleEditor, AssetClasses -- now clear every one of this group's contract criteria, including its two raised bars (accessibility >=7, interaction_feedback >=7).
